text.p: Isolyser Co Inc said Thursday it expects to report a loss for the 1996 fourth quarter.
It did not give a specific projection, saying it would release results for the quarter in late February after a final accounting.
For the 1995 fourth quarter the company reported a loss of $0.03 a share on net sales of $28.3 million.
Isolyser shares were down 1-3/8 at 5-1/2 in late-morning trading.
Isolyser said it was recording significant reserves against the early generation of its OREX product, which was deemed obsolete by improved manufacturing processes.
The recording of reserves will also provide for the divestiture of certain non-core businesses, it said.

"As a part of reviewing and addressing our concerns about 1996 performance, we are focusing on our core business and thoroughly reviewing our operational structure for possible cost-saving opportunities," it said.

Isolyser, based in Norcross, Ga., develops and manufactures OREX Degradables, a series of products made from a thermoplastic, hot-water-soluble polymer that can be configured into an array of products such as woven and non-woven fabrics, film and thermoformed and extruded items.
